title: Skills routing
blurb: Queues, the awkward tab name, pools, levels, Default, and the scoreboard.
summary: A skill is people plus a place on the campaign. Default is what you get when you forget.

lessons.title: A skill is a queue with people in it
objectives: Set a service level you can explain
paragraphs: A skill group holds users who have the agent or supervisor role. Campaigns point at one or more groups. The people, not the name, determine who can receive the contact.
Service level, voicemail, greetings, and a message to the group are all on the skill topic. A skill with no members is a label.

lessons.title: The tab is named backwards on inbound
paragraphs: Outbound campaigns take skills on the Skills tab. Inbound and autodial take them on a tab named Outbound Skills. The skill topic says this in one paragraph. People miss it because the word outbound sits on an inbound campaign.
If the right people are Ready and the queue is still empty, look at the tab before you look at the carrier.

lessons.title: One module, one skill, when you need the truth
objectives: Choose pool or precision out loud
Match the report to that choice
paragraphs: Skill Transfer may list several skills, and any agent who has one of them can take the call. The same article recommends a single skill in the module when you want reports that mean something.
A shared pool is a valid design. An accidental shared pool is how billing calls show up as a blob. Split modules if the work is different. Keep one module if the pool is the point.

lessons.title: Skill level versus list order
objectives: Pick list order or agent level
paragraphs: The skill transfer article describes an option to ignore the order of skills in the module and distribute by the agent's skill level instead. Order and level are different ideas. Order is the list you typed. Level is a property of the agent.
This lab does not quote the click-path for editing an agent's level. If you use the option, confirm in the editor which number wins. Do not assume the top of the list is the highest level.
uncertain: The article names the option. The exact screen where an agent's skill level is edited was not quoted in this lab.

lessons.title: Default is a queue, not a compliment
objectives: Name a skill on every transfer
paragraphs: If Skill Transfer has no skill selected, the article says calls go to users who are not assigned skills. That queue is labeled Default in the softphone. It is a catch-all, not a place you want billing calls.
Supervisors and agents with empty skill lists become the Default pool. An empty list is easy to create when a user profile is cloned and skills are forgotten.

lessons.title: Service level is the scoreboard
objectives: Set a service level you mean
Do not move it to hide a miss
paragraphs: The skill topic includes service levels. A service level answers 'how fast is acceptable,' usually as a percent of contacts answered inside a number of seconds. It does not, by itself, reorder the queue. Priority does the ordering. The scoreboard tells you if the ordering and the staffing worked.
A blend that steals agents will miss the inbound service level even when the skill is configured perfectly. The scoreboard is how you prove the steal rule.

figure.title: Scoreboard versus steering
figure.caption: Do not turn the scoreboard to steer.

steps.title: Cause

steps.title: Avoid

steps.title: Staff

lessons.title: Skill voicemail is its own mailbox
objectives: Give skill voicemail its own greeting
paragraphs: The skill topic covers routing voicemail to the group, greetings, messages, and audio files. That mailbox is not the campaign Play prompt and not an agent's personal phone mailbox unless you have built it that way.
Queue callback, on Skill Transfer, is yet another path, with its own disposition advice: the article says the default disposition is Abandon and tells you to create callback-specific codes.
